name: Ballpit-TS-TW

frames.best_why: Spheres are scattered through the air over a settled pile with the heading still readable.

tagline: Grey and white spheres tumble, bounce and pile up like a ball pit.
summary: A 3D physics toy of dozens of glossy spheres in white, grey and graphite that fall, collide and settle into a heap on a black stage. Moving the cursor pushes them around.
appearance: A black stage holds a heap of glossy 3D spheres in white, light grey and dark graphite, of mixed sizes, piled along the bottom and drifting upward. A bright white glow forms in the middle of the pile, and a white 'Ballpit' heading with a small grey subtitle floats near the top.
behaviour: Gravity pulls the spheres down so they bounce off the floor and walls and shove each other, then settle into a loose heap. Moving the cursor drags an invisible control sphere that knocks them around before they calm again.
demo_content: A white heading 'Ballpit' with the line 'Move your cursor to push the spheres around.'
search_phrases: white spheres that react to the mouse
balls pile up at the bottom of the screen
use_when: You want a playful, physics-driven 3D backdrop for a hero or landing page that responds to the pointer.
avoid_when: It is a continuous simulation with hundreds of collision checks per frame, heavy on low-end phones.
customise: Props pass count, colours, gravity, friction, wall bounce, sphere sizes, material and light settings, plus the follow-cursor toggle. The demo heading and subtitle are separate page markup.
weight_why: 140 spheres with pairwise collision checks and a Three.js render loop on every frame.

a11y.note: The physics keeps moving forever and ignores reduced-motion; the canvas has no label or pause control.

issues: The demo heading sits behind the spheres and gets hidden when they fly upward.
The simulation never pauses for reduced-motion and the demo offers no pause control.
Hundreds of pairwise sphere collisions per frame make it heavy on phones.
polish_why: Convincing glossy spheres and lively physics, but the greys are flat and the heading collides.
